answer: A new identity starts at the bottom of a reputation ladder, far from the harbor of high-value work: it may only take tasks worth at most 5 units and must finish 20 verified jobs over 14 days before its cap rises. Each completed job is an anchor in its public work history, signed by three randomly chosen verifiers before payment releases. An attacker who tries to wander across ten fake identities must complete 200 real jobs and wait the full fortnight for each, while splitting attention lowers every pass rate; the ledger enforces caps and signatures, so fakes cannot shortcut to valuable tasks.
